definitions.explanation: An organism, typically bacteria or fungi, that breaks down dead organic matter and returns nutrients to the ecosystem.

examples.japanese: キノコ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{分解者|ぶんかいしゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Mushrooms are one type of decomposer.

examples.japanese: {分解者|ぶんかいしゃ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{生態系|せいたいけい}→生態系：04626_seitaikei⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{重要|じゅうよう}→重要：01575_juuyou⟧な⟦{役割|やくわり}を{果|は}たす→役割を果たす：19503_yakuwariwohatasu⟧。
examples.english: Decomposers play an important role in ecosystems.

examples.japanese: {分解者|ぶんかいしゃ}がいなければ、⟦{落|お}ち{葉|ば}→落ち葉：14108_ochiba⟧や⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{死骸|しがい}→死骸：28379_shigai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{分解|ぶんかい}されない→分解する：21320_bunkaisuru⟧。
examples.english: Without decomposers, fallen leaves and animal carcasses would not be broken down.

notes:
{分解者|ぶんかいしゃ} is a biology term composed of ⟦{分解|ぶんかい}→分解：08389_bunkai⟧ (decomposition) + ⟦{者|しゃ}→〜者：04662_sha⟧ (one who does). It refers to organisms that break down dead organic matter, recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.

ECOSYSTEM ROLES (commonly taught as a set):
- ⟦{生産者|せいさんしゃ}→生産者：25443_seisansha⟧: producer (plants — make food via photosynthesis)
- ⟦{消費者|しょうひしゃ}→消費者：09866_shouhisha⟧: consumer (animals — eat other organisms)
- {分解者|ぶんかいしゃ}: decomposer (break down dead matter)

EXAMPLES OF DECOMPOSERS:
- ⟦{細菌|さいきん}→細菌：13791_saikin⟧: bacteria
- ⟦{菌類|きんるい}→菌類：20139_kinrui⟧: fungi (including mushrooms and mold)
- ミミズ: earthworms

USAGE:
This term appears frequently in ⟦{理科|りか}→理科：03994_rika⟧ (science) classes and ⟦{生態系|せいたいけい}→生態系：04626_seitaikei⟧ (ecosystem) discussions. The three-role classification is a standard part of Japanese science education.
